# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-reference.sh from `pando --version`: pando 3.4.0. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every `pando` command and option, as printed by `--help`. For a task-by-task guide, start with [Try it in 5 minutes](../getting-started.md); for git equivalents, see [Coming from git](../git-users.md).

## `pando clone`

```text
Create a workspace and check out a ref (lazily, and sparsely with --path)

Usage: pando clone [OPTIONS] <SERVER> <DIR>

Arguments:
  <SERVER>
  <DIR>

Options:
      --ref <REF_NAME>     [default: main]
      --token <TOKEN>      Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --path <PATHS>       Only materialise these paths (repeatable)
      --objects <OBJECTS>  Fetch objects through a node daemon or regional cache [env: PANDO_OBJECTS=]
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## `pando commit`

```text

Options:

      --token <TOKEN>      Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
  -h, --help               Print help

```

## `pando mount`

```text
Mount a revision read-only; files are fetched on first read (Linux, macOS, Windows)

Usage: pando mount [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>

Options:
      --server <SERVER>
      --token <TOKEN>        Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --objects <OBJECTS>    Daemon or cache serving objects
      --rev <REV>            [default: main]
      --cache-mb <CACHE_MB>  In-memory cache for file contents [default: 256]
      --serve-only           Serve the checkout over NFS on localhost and print the command that mounts it, instead of mounting (for machines where only an administrator may mount, or Linux machines without FUSE)
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

## `pando mcp`

```text
Serve Pando as MCP tools over stdio for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor...)

Usage: pando mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --server <SERVER>

      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --http <ADDR>
          Serve the whole server to remote agents over HTTP at this address (e.g. 0.0.0.0:7430), instead of one workspace over stdio. Each request's bearer token is passed through to the server
      --allowed-host <ALLOWED_HOSTS>
          Host names clients use to reach the HTTP endpoint (repeatable); default: loopback only, against DNS rebinding
      --allowed-origin <ALLOWED_ORIGINS>
          Browser origins allowed to call the HTTP endpoint (repeatable), e.g. https://app.example.com:443; default: none (requests with an Origin are refused)
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `pando repo`

```text
Create and list repositories on a server that hosts many (`pandod server --platform`)

Usage: pando repo [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create  Create OWNER/NAME. Then: `pando clone SERVER/OWNER/NAME`
  list    List repositories, optionally of one owner
  grant   Give a person, agent or team (ORG/TEAM) a role on a repository; `none` removes it. With only the repository, lists who has access
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --token <TOKEN>  Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

### `pando repo create`

```text
Create OWNER/NAME. Then: `pando clone SERVER/OWNER/NAME`

Usage: pando repo create [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>

Options:
      --description <DESCRIPTION>  [default: ""]
      --token <TOKEN>              Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --server <SERVER>
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version
```

### `pando repo list`

```text
List repositories, optionally of one owner

Usage: pando repo list [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --owner <OWNER>    [default: ""]
      --token <TOKEN>    Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --server <SERVER>
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### `pando repo grant`

```text
Give a person, agent or team (ORG/TEAM) a role on a repository; `none` removes it. With only the repository, lists who has access

Usage: pando repo grant [OPTIONS] <REPO> [PRINCIPAL] [ROLE]

Arguments:
  <REPO>


  [PRINCIPAL]


  [ROLE]
          Possible values:
          - read
          - triage
          - write
          - maintain
          - admin
          - none:     Removes the member or grant

Options:
      --server <SERVER>


      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved

          [env: PANDO_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `pando cr`

```text
Change requests: propose a branch, review it, land it

Usage: pando cr [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create   Propose a branch for landing on another: `pando cr create --title "…"`
  list     List change requests
  view     Show one, with what still blocks it
  comment  Comment, on the change or on a line of a file
  review   Approve, request changes, or comment
  check    Report a CI check on the current version: `pando cr check 12 build passed --url …`
  land     Land it, once nothing blocks it
  rebase   Replay it on the target's tip
  ready    Mark a draft ready for review
  close
  reopen
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --server <SERVER>  The repository, SERVER/OWNER/NAME; defaults to the workspace's
      --token <TOKEN>    Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### `pando cr create`

```text
Propose a branch for landing on another: `pando cr create --title "…"`

Usage: pando cr create [OPTIONS] --title <TITLE>

Options:
      --server <SERVER>       The repository, SERVER/OWNER/NAME; defaults to the workspace's
      --title <TITLE>
      --token <TOKEN>         Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --body <BODY>           [default: ""]
      --source <SOURCE>       The branch to land; defaults to the workspace's branch
      --target <TARGET>       Where to land it; defaults to the repository's default branch [default: ""]
      --draft
      --reviewer <REVIEWERS>  Ask someone to review (repeatable)
  -h, --help                  Print help
  -V, --version               Print version
```

      --author <AUTHOR>  Only this author; `agent/*` for every agent [default: ""]

### `pando token create`

```text
Create a token. Prints it once: store it as PANDO_TOKEN

Usage: pando token create [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
      --as <ACTS_AS>
          Act as an agent you answer for, e.g. `agent/refactor-07` (created if new)

      --server <SERVER>


      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved

          [env: PANDO_TOKEN]

      --repo <REPOSITORIES>
          Only these repositories, OWNER/NAME (repeatable); default: all you can reach

      --role <ROLE>
          Highest role the token may use

          Possible values:
          - read
          - triage
          - write
          - maintain
          - admin
          - none:     Removes the member or grant

          [default: write]

      --days <DAYS>
          Days until it expires (1–366)

          [default: 90]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `pando migrate`

```text
Move a repository from any git host to Pando: full history, and from GitHub, open pull requests (as change requests) and issues with their comments

Usage: pando migrate [OPTIONS] --to <TO> <FROM>

Arguments:
  <FROM>  Where it is now: any URL git can clone

Options:
      --to <TO>
          Where it goes: SERVER/OWNER/NAME
      --token <TOKEN>
          Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --github-token <GITHUB_TOKEN>
          For private GitHub repositories, and to avoid GitHub's rate limit. Prefer the PANDO_GITHUB_TOKEN (or GITHUB_TOKEN) environment variable or --github-token-file: a value given here is visible to other users of the machine (`ps`) [env: PANDO_GITHUB_TOKEN]
      --github-token-file <GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE>
          Read the GitHub token from this file
      --no-issues
          Skip issues
      --no-pull-requests
          Skip pull requests
      --github-api <GITHUB_API>
          GitHub Enterprise Server's API, e.g. https://github.example.com/api/v3
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `pando mirror`

```text
Keep a git repository (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, any git remote) up to date with a branch: every landed change becomes the same git commit every time, pushed without force

Usage: pando mirror [OPTIONS] --to <TO>

Options:
      --to <TO>            Where to push: any URL git accepts. Credentials come from git (SSH keys or a credential helper)
      --token <TOKEN>      Bearer token for the server ($PANDO_TOKEN); without one, the token `pando login` saved [env: PANDO_TOKEN]
      --server <SERVER>
      --rev <REV>          [default: main]
      --git-ref <GIT_REF>  [default: main]
      --dir <DIR>          The mirror's local copy (a bare git repository); defaults to the user cache
      --every <SECONDS>    Mirror again every SECONDS until interrupted; without it, mirror once and exit
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```
